purpose: One solution-neutral Direction comparison fixture. It defines equivalent content, roles, states, environments, and observations for every territory; it is not participant evidence or an approved study plan.

sourceDeck.use: Candidate IDs only; editorial approval is required before any participant use.

playable.requiredMix: Two authentic and two fabricated-for-game cards at short, median, and maximum approved statement/attribution lengths.
constraints: Use difficult attributions and sensitive-but-allowed material only after two-person editorial review.
Use the same seeded order, card text, attribution, timer, answer labels, and score semantics in all territories.
Do not use a disputed, source-unavailable, or removed record as a binary playable card.

roleScripts: Forehead group: screen-facing participants read and discuss; holder commits one group answer by tilt or tap without perceiving the active statement.
Pass-and-play: current player privately reads and commits; score belongs to that player or team; protected handoff hides prior card and outcome.

Screen-reader contribution: a screen-reader participant may be the screen-facing contributor in forehead play or complete private pass-and-play; a forehead holder must never receive the active statement through speech, audio route, haptic, interruption, or handoff.

environment.phoneSizes: Freeze one small and one large representative iOS/Android device before prototype production.
environment.viewing: Freeze primary and stress viewing distances, angles, and maximum platform text size before the study plan is signed.

safetyChecks: pre-reveal capture retains game context without authenticity leakage
protected handoff does not leak prior content
queued report and debug/analytics proposals respect the data-minimization allowlist

freezeRule: Any participant study must bind this file's SHA-256 into a signed independent-study plan. Changing a card, state, role script, access path, environment, or observation requires a new fixture digest and new plan signature.
